meta.title: ISDS Thematic Watcher — how the whole thing works
meta.note: v2.1 (operator revisions 2026-07-29): Emory naming, per-agent models + training lines, substantive plain language, badge layout fix, Bing News in / Google News retired, delivery legend reworded.

nodes.title: Runs by itself every Monday
nodes.desc: A scheduled timer starts the whole pipeline — nobody has to remember.
nodes.meta: GitHub Actions schedule — deterministic, no model involved

nodes.title: Collect everything new
nodes.desc: Pulls this week's listings from all 9 sources above into one pile.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code (no AI) — src/sources/

nodes.title: Skip repeats
nodes.desc: A memory file remembers every item ever seen, so nothing is processed twice.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code (no AI) — state/seen.json

nodes.title: First scoring pass
nodes.desc: Counts legal key-phrases (the three 'rings') for a quick relevance score.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code (no AI) — fingerprint.yaml weights

nodes.title: Read the document
nodes.desc: Fetches each promising item and pulls out its single most quotable line.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code (no AI) — src/enrich.py

nodes.title: AI relevance check
nodes.desc: Claude reads each item and scores its relevance to the research question, with reasons.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude Haiku 4.5 — strict structured output; falls back to the keyword score

nodes.title: Quality bar
nodes.desc: Items scoring 40+ enter the digest. Near-misses (25+) may fill a quiet week, always labeled as leads.
nodes.meta: Deterministic rule — threshold 40, floor 25, no exceptions

nodes.title: Daily research email
nodes.desc: Each day's meeting record, emailed to Emory with the numbers-of-record banner.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code — includes the numbers-of-record banner

nodes.title: Weekly digest email
nodes.desc: The annotated reading list of this week's finds — sent to Dr. Benavides.
nodes.meta: Deterministic render of the scored items — no model writes the digest

nodes.title: Public website
nodes.desc: The digest archive and methodology, published automatically to the project site.
nodes.meta: Deterministic build — drift-guarded against the repo

nodes.title: Research brief email
nodes.desc: The council's plain-English interpretation of the week — sent to Dr. Benavides.
nodes.meta: Written by the council, sent by deterministic code

nodes.title: Monday review packet
nodes.desc: Emory's Monday briefing: council minutes and grades, workflow ideas, the state of the answer, and claims needing his check.
nodes.meta: Assembled by deterministic code from the week's records

nodes.title: Daily researcher
nodes.desc: Meets every day: works the open questions and logs at most one genuinely new, sourced insight.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude (scheduled daily routine) — bound by the council calibration checklist

nodes.title: Chairman
nodes.desc: Sets the weekly agenda from the open questions and directs where the analyst spends effort.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude Fable 5 — standing role prompt (council_chairman.txt)

nodes.title: Analyst
nodes.desc: Interprets the week against the research question with bounded web research; proposes claims with exact quotes.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude Opus 4.8 — role prompt + the no-source-no-claim rule

nodes.title: Systems researcher
nodes.desc: Studies the instrument itself and proposes one sourced improvement at a time.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude (daily routine) — systems_researcher.txt prompt

nodes.title: Editor
nodes.desc: Writes the reader-facing brief. May state as fact only what survived the gates.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude Opus 4.8 — structured-output contract (strict JSON schema)

nodes.title: Meeting minutes
nodes.desc: The chairman reviews each member's week on the record: status, grades, next steps, escalations to Emory.
nodes.meta: Model: Claude Fable 5 — reconvene prompt; fail-loud if minutes are missing

nodes.title: The living memory — 'State of the Answer'
nodes.desc: The cumulative answer and every open question are saved and feed next Monday's agenda — research compounds.
nodes.meta: Files: STATE_OF_THE_ANSWER.md + state/research_log.json

nodes.title: Emory verifies facts
nodes.desc: Each claim is checked against its original source. Emory confirms or rejects it — the system cannot verify facts itself.
nodes.meta: Human judgment — the one step no model is allowed to perform

nodes.title: Verified-facts ledger
nodes.desc: A permanent record of every claim and its status. Events are only ever added, so nothing can be quietly rewritten.
nodes.meta: Append-only file — analytics/verification_ledger.jsonl

nodes.title: Claim gate (automatic)
nodes.desc: Code looks up every claim in the ledger by exact ID. Unverified claims must be labeled as leads; rejected ones are blocked.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code (no AI) — src/integrity_gate.py

nodes.title: Citation check (automatic)
nodes.desc: A checking program opens every cited link to confirm it exists and is reachable; unlinked citations are flagged for Emory.
nodes.meta: Deterministic code (no AI) — scripts/check_citations.py

edges.evidence: daily optimization ideas feed the systems log
citation verdict attached to the brief
improvement queue lands in the close-out
reconvene runs on the finished brief
